"There is nothing technical in the word as used."

"it seems sufficient if it be in writing and signed by him, unless a seal is expressly required by a particular act of Parliament," ...; "sec. 1993 of which the requisites and form of warrant ... are given, the form being attested 'under hand' but not 'under seal.'"

“it surely cannot be necessary now to say that the validity of a legislative act depends, in no degree, on its containing the technical terms used in a conveyance. Nothing can be more apparent than the intention of the legislature …”
“the word "book" as used in the statute is not to be understood in its technical sense of a bound volume, but any species of publication which the author selects to embody his literary product.”

"Nor should the particular language of the article above set out be given a narrow or hypercritical meaning."

"We attach little value to this logical concatenation as against the direct effect of 64, taken according to the normal usages of speech."

“the Court gives the phrase judicial review in [§]10 a technical content… If anything is plain in the legislative history of the Administrative Procedure Act it is that the Congress was not concerned with formularies when it referred to statutes which preclude judicial review.”

"In sum, the statutory language does not suggest that it covers only common-law larceny."

“Where the question we face is what meaning Congress attached to a particular word or phrase, we usually and properly are loath to conclude that Congress meant to use the word or phrase in a hypertechnical sense unless it said so.”
